description.narrative:
The Middle East needs inclusive security structures, and an overall security structure for the region may not be realized in the short term. Yet, the project aims to focus on the essential building blocks of a cooperative security regime regardless of prevailing regional circumstances. The project aims to: 1- Identify threat perceptions & security challenges in the region: This is to be achieved by analyzing main drivers for regional instability and insecurity, how countries define their threats, how countries react to a threat, analyze the performance of regional alliances and why challenges/complications in the Middle East are still unresolved. 2- Introduce main pillars (or building blocks) to be considered in a future regional security formulation: The Middle East faces grave challenges, a significant number of these challenges are of techno-strategic nature including the proliferation of missile capabilities, growing nuclear ambitions and instability in the maritime field. The "building blocks approach" discusses the main pillars of a regional security system in the Middle East region, it promotes practical solutions with a focus on maritime, missiles and nuclear capabilities.
The following outcomes are expected: - Hold a regional dialogue session with Jordanian, Saudi, and Iranian participation. - Present project initial findings at the Amman Security Colloquium, this includes a youth component. - Launching regional consultations on the impact of missiles on regional stability. - Introducing confidence building measures and paving the way for a non-aggression pact. - Launch white paper titled "set of principles for a regional security structure". - Produce a short video trailer on project outcomes.
